name: Documentation Update or Create
description: Survey existing docs, approve the update or create scope, draft new or updated content, validate all links and code examples, gate, then polish. Best for API docs, READMEs, guides, inline comments, and adding brand-new doc files.

steps.title: Survey Existing Docs
steps.prompt_template:
You are a technical writer performing a documentation audit.

Documentation target: {{feature_description}}
Repositories in scope: {{repo_list}}

## Intent
First, decide the Intent of this request based on `{{feature_description}}`:
- **create** — the user wants brand-new documentation files written (e.g. "document the new auth flow", "add a guide for X"). No pre-existing file is implied; pick sensible new paths under `docs/`.
- **update** — the user wants changes to documentation files that already exist (e.g. "refresh the README", "fix typos in the API docs").
- **mixed** — both create and update (e.g. "document the new auth flow and update the README to link to it").
State the chosen Intent at the top of your output. The downstream `s-draft` step will use this to decide whether to create new files or edit existing ones.

## Your task
Survey all documentation related to the target. If Intent is **create** or **mixed**, identify both existing files that need updating AND new files that need to be authored. If Intent is **update**, focus on existing files only.

## Operating boundary (ANALYSIS mode)
You are operating in ANALYSIS mode for this step. The orchestrator's chmod fence restricts writes to `artifacts/` only. You may ONLY write your output to `artifacts/s-survey.md` — do NOT create or modify anything under `docs/` yourself. The actual file creation/editing happens in the later `s-draft` step which has `implement` capability.

## Required sections
1. **Intent** — one of: create | update | mixed.
2. **Files to Update** — table: file path | current state | what will change | priority (High/Medium/Low). May be empty when Intent is `create`.
3. **Files to Create** — table: file path | purpose | rationale (what new doc will cover) | priority (High/Medium/Low). May be empty when Intent is `update`.
4. **Style & Voice Reference** — identify the existing tone, tense, and formatting conventions from the best-written existing doc in the repo. When Intent is `create`, also note any nearby doc whose style the new file should match.
5. **Link Inventory** — all internal and external links in the docs that will change. Flag any already-broken links.
6. **Code Examples** — list all code examples in scope. Flag examples that are likely outdated.
7. **Proposed Scope** — a conservative list of exactly which files will be touched and what will change (both update and create paths). Do not include nice-to-haves. Every file in 'Files to Update' AND 'Files to Create' must appear here exactly as listed.

## Stop condition
You are done when all 7 sections are present, the Intent is declared, every file in 'Files to Update' and 'Files to Create' has a stated priority, and 'Proposed Scope' lists every file the next step will touch (created or updated). The 'Proposed Scope' must be the complete, authoritative file list for `s-draft`.

Write your complete output to `artifacts/s-survey.md`.

steps.title: Approve Documentation Scope
steps.prompt_template: Review the Survey artifact from 's-survey'. The Proposed Scope may include both updates to existing documentation files AND brand-new documentation files that will be authored from scratch (see the survey's 'Intent' and 'Files to Create' sections). Approve the proposed scope to begin drafting. Redirect to narrow or expand the scope — your feedback will adjust the draft's focus. Cancel to abort.

steps.title: Draft Updated Documentation
steps.prompt_template:
You are a technical writer updating documentation.

Documentation target (create or update): {{feature_description}}
Survey artifact: [attached — from s-survey]
Gate scope feedback: {{gate_feedback}}

## Capability note
This step runs with `implement` capability. The orchestrator's chmod fence from the survey step is lifted, so you may freely create new files under `docs/` (e.g. `docs/AUTH.md`) in addition to editing existing ones. Filesystem access is still scoped to your worktree.

## Rules
1. Write in the style and voice documented in the survey's 'Style & Voice Reference' section. Match tense, heading style, and tone exactly. For new files, mirror the style of the closest existing doc flagged in the survey.
2. Author ONLY the files in the approved 'Proposed Scope' — create new files at the approved paths, update existing files in place; do not touch any other file.
3. Add or update code examples where they improve clarity — mark new examples with an `<!-- EXAMPLE: new -->` comment.
4. Do NOT break existing markdown anchors (e.g., `#section-name`) without updating all references to them.
5. Do NOT update links that are not in the survey's Link Inventory unless they are obviously broken.

## On Retry (only when retry feedback is present)
If the following feedback is non-empty, this is attempt {{iteration}} of {{max_iterations}} — validation failed previously:
{{retry_feedback}}
Focus exclusively on resolving what the feedback describes (e.g. broken links, failing examples); do not redo unrelated work. If the feedback is empty, this is the first attempt — ignore this section.

## Output artifact
- List of files written (created + updated)
- New or updated sections (summary)
- Code examples added/updated (list)
- Links updated (list)

## Stop condition
You are done when every file in the approved scope has been written — both the 'Files to Create' entries (new files) and the 'Files to Update' entries (existing files).

steps.title: Validate Links & Code Examples
steps.prompt_template:
You are a documentation QA engineer performing a technical validation pass.

Draft artifact: [attached — from s-draft]
Survey link inventory: [attached — from s-survey]

## Validation checklist
1. **Internal links** — verify every internal markdown link resolves to an existing heading or file. List broken links.
2. **External links** — check the links from the survey's Link Inventory that were updated. Verify they resolve correctly.
3. **Code examples** — for every `<!-- EXAMPLE: new -->` example added: attempt to compile or run it. Report pass/fail per example.
4. **Anchor integrity** — list any heading that was renamed or removed; flag if there are stale references elsewhere in the docs.

## Output artifact
- Broken internal links: list (should be empty)
- Broken external links: list
- Code example results: example | PASS / FAIL / NOT TESTED
- Stale anchors: list
- **Verdict: VALID / INVALID**

## Stop condition
You are done when all 4 checklist items are assessed and a Verdict is stated.

Write your complete output to `artifacts/s-validate.md`.

verifier.instructions: Decide whether the documentation update is correct and complete. Base your verdict primarily on the validation results (broken links, failing code examples, stale anchors, and the VALID/INVALID verdict); treat any harness output above as secondary. Return "pass" only if there are no broken internal links and no failing code examples; otherwise return "fail" with a concise, actionable reason naming exactly what to fix.

steps.title: Review Draft Documentation
steps.prompt_template: Review the Draft artifact (s-draft) and the Validation report (s-validate). Remember that the draft may contain both newly-created documentation files and updates to existing ones — review both kinds. If Validation shows INVALID, redirect to fix the broken items first. If VALID: approve to begin the final polish pass. Cancel to abort.

steps.title: Polish & Finalise
steps.prompt_template:
You are a technical writer doing a final polish pass.

Gate feedback: {{gate_feedback}}
Draft artifact: [attached — from s-draft]
Validation artifact: [attached — from s-validate]

## Tasks
1. Apply all reviewer feedback from the gate decision.
2. Fix all INVALID items from the validation report (broken links, failing examples).
3. Final style pass: consistent heading capitalisation, no trailing whitespace, no double blank lines.
4. Write a CHANGELOG entry summarising the documentation changes for this feature.

## Output artifact
- Gate feedback items resolved: list
- Validation issues resolved: list
- CHANGELOG entry (copy-paste ready)

## Stop condition
You are done when all gate feedback and validation issues are resolved and the CHANGELOG entry is written.
